answer: Latency fingerprint clustering. Each agent signs every action with a timestamp; the system logs inter-action gaps and builds a per-identity timing profile. Sybils run from one operator share scheduler artifacts, so gaps correlate far above the population nadir of natural variance. When a cluster of identities shows correlated gaps, all are quarantined into a review haven pending re-verification. An attacker must then inject independent random delays and separate hosts per identity—a juniper-thin margin of extra operational cost per account, scaled across thousands of identities.
